filters.name: Parametrize from Registered Rasters
filters.shortDescription: The mesh is parameterized by creating some patches that correspond to projection of portions of surfaces onto the set of registered rasters.
filters.longDescriptionMarkdown:
The mesh is parameterized by creating patches that correspond to projections of surface portions onto the set of registered rasters. For each face, a reference raster is chosen based on visibility, viewing angle, and optional weights. Connected faces sharing the same reference raster form patches. UV coordinates are computed by projecting faces onto the reference raster's image plane. Patches are then packed into texture space using rectangle packing.

Requires at least one visible raster with a valid camera and a 2-manifold mesh.

parameters.label: Use distance weight
parameters.help: Includes a weight accounting for the distance to the camera during the computation of reference images.

parameters.label: Use image border weight
parameters.help: Includes a weight accounting for the distance to the image border during the computation of reference images.

parameters.label: Use image alpha weight
parameters.help: If true, alpha channel of the image is used as additional weight. Makes it possible to mask-out parts of images that should not be projected on the mesh.

parameters.label: Clean isolated triangles
parameters.help: Remove all patches composed of a single triangle by aggregating them to adjacent patches.

parameters.label: UV stretching
parameters.help: If true, texture coordinates are stretched to cover the full [0,1] interval for both directions.

parameters.label: Texture gutter
parameters.help: Extra boundary to add to each patch before packing in texture space (in pixels).

parameters.label: Depth epsilon
parameters.help: Tolerance for depth test when checking vertex visibility against the software depth buffer. Increasing this value merges similar-depth regions, reducing the number of patches. Use values of a few units for noisy or inaccurate camera registrations.

parameters.label: Max packing grid size
parameters.help: Maximum dimension of the packing grid (in pixels). Set to 0 to auto-compute from the total patch area. Lower values speed up packing but may produce denser, lower-resolution layouts.

filters.name: Parametrize from Registered Rasters with Texture
filters.shortDescription: The mesh is parameterized and textured by creating some patches that correspond to projection of portions of surfaces onto the set of registered rasters.
filters.longDescriptionMarkdown:
The mesh is parameterized and textured by creating patches that correspond to projections of surface portions onto the set of registered rasters. After patch-based parameterization, a texture image is generated by painting each raster into the corresponding UV regions. Optionally, a color correction step ensures seamless transitions between adjacent patches.

Requires at least one visible raster with a valid camera and a 2-manifold mesh.

parameters.label: Texture Size
parameters.help: The side of the generated texture, which is square, in texels.

parameters.label: Texture name
parameters.help: Name of the new texture, which is also its file name when the mesh is saved. Leave it empty to name it after the layer.

parameters.label: Color correction
parameters.help: If true, the final texture is corrected to ensure seamless transitions between adjacent patches.

parameters.label: Color correction filter
parameters.help: Radius (in pixels) of the kernel used to compute the difference between corresponding texels in different rasters. Default of 1 generates a 3x3 kernel. Higher values increase robustness for strong misalignments.

parameters.label: Use distance weight
parameters.help: Includes a weight accounting for the distance to the camera during the computation of reference images.

parameters.label: Use image border weight
parameters.help: Includes a weight accounting for the distance to the image border during the computation of reference images.

parameters.label: Use image alpha weight
parameters.help: If true, alpha channel of the image is used as additional weight. Makes it possible to mask-out parts of images that should not be projected on the mesh.

parameters.label: UV stretching

filters.name: Compute Vertex Scalar from Raster Coverage
filters.shortDescription: Compute a quality value representing the number of images into which each vertex of the active mesh is visible.
filters.longDescriptionMarkdown: Compute a quality value representing the number of images into which each vertex of the active mesh is visible. For each active raster, a software depth buffer is built and each vertex is tested for visibility (inside the image bounds, front-facing, and passing the depth test). The quality value counts how many rasters each vertex is visible in. Optionally normalizes to [0,1].

parameters.label: Normalize
parameters.help: Rescale quality values to the range [0,1].

parameters.label: Depth epsilon
parameters.help: Tolerance for depth test when checking vertex visibility. Increase for noisy registrations.

filters.name: Compute Face Scalar from Rasters
filters.shortDescription: Measure, for each face, how well the visible rasters see it: how many, at what resolution, at what angle, or how much of that resolution its texture keeps.
filters.longDescriptionMarkdown:
Measures, for each face, how well the visible rasters cover it, so that a photo set can be checked before it is used for texturing or color transfer. The result is a per-face scalar, shown with the colormap.

A raster **sees** a face when at least two of three points inside it (at barycentric coordinates (2/3, 1/6, 1/6) and its permutations) project inside the image, in front of the camera, on the front side of the face, and pass a depth test against a software depth buffer of the whole mesh. This asks whether most of the face is visible: a single sample at a vertex or at the centroid decides a half-hidden face by chance.

**Measure** chooses what is written:

- **Count**: how many rasters see the face.
- **Best resolution**: over the rasters that see the face, the largest square root of its projected area in pixels over its area on the mesh. It is a linear density, in pixels per document unit (pixels per centimeter when the document unit is centimeters), and it falls both with distance and with foreshortening.
- **Best angle**: over the rasters that see the face, the smallest angle in degrees between the face normal and the direction to the camera. It separates faces seen only at grazing angles from faces seen head-on from too far away.
- **Texture/photo ratio**: the texel density of the face in the layer's own texture (as *Compute UV Distortion* measures it, in texels per document unit) over its best resolution. Below 1 the texture keeps less detail than the best photo of the face offers, above 1 it spends texels the photos cannot fill. It needs a texture coordinate layer and its texture images (only their sizes are read); a face without texture gets 0.

Faces that no raster sees get 0 for Count, Best resolution and Texture/photo ratio, and 180 for Best angle.

The run also reports the minimum, median and 5th percentile of the measure over the faces that some raster sees, and how many faces no raster sees and how many only one raster sees.

parameters.label: Measure
parameters.help: What to write for each face: how many rasters see it, the best resolution any of them gives it in pixels per document unit, the smallest angle in degrees between its normal and a camera that sees it, or its texel density in the layer's texture over that best resolution.

parameters.label: Depth epsilon
parameters.help: Tolerance for the depth test, in document units, when checking whether a point of a face is hidden. Increase for noisy registrations.
